 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.

  3
 Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

 SUBJECT:  ADOPTION  OF  FISCAL  YEAR  2022-2023  MUNICIPAL  BUDGETS  AND  5-
 YEAR  CAPIT  AL  IMPROVEMENT  PROGRAM  FOR  THE  CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE;  SOUTH
 GATE  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  AND  THE  SUCCESSOR  AGENCY  TO  THE  COMMUNITY
 DEVELOPMENT  COMMISSION  OF THE  CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE

 PURPOSE:  To hear budget  presentations  from  staff  and review  the Proposed  Fiscal  Year  2022-23
 Municipal  Budget  for these various  entities  and consider  the adoption  of the proposed  spending  plan(s)
 as indicated  in the Resolution  attached  for consideration.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council,  South  Gate Housing  Authority  and the Successor
 Agency  to the Cornrnunity  Development  Commission  of the City  of South Gate will  consider:

  a.  Hearing  the various  presentations  on the Proposed  Fiscal  Year  2022-23  Municipal  Budget  and
  5-Year  Capital  Improvement  Program  for the various  entities;  and

  b.  Approving  a Resolution  adopting  the  Municipal  Budget  for  Fiscal  Year  2022-23  with  the
  changes  stipulated  in Exhibit  A  for  a total  of  $243,580,301  for  all  funds  along  with  any
  additions  or deletions  the Legislatiye  Bodies  may enact.

  c.  Approving  a Resolution  adopting  the  annual  Gann  Appropriations  Limit  for  Fiscal  Year
  2022/23.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  The Proposed  Budget  for Fiscal  Year  2022-23,  to include  all fiinds  and entities,
 as amended  is $243,580,301.  This  amount  includes  transfers  in and out of various  funds.  The General
 Fund accounts  for $65,612,875  including  transfers  out. The Proposed  Budget  for the Successor  Agency
 is $5,012,976  and the Housing  Authority  is $5,174,549.  The total  revenue  estimated  for all entities  and
 funds  is $184,243,818.  The differences  are covered  by the reserves  and/or  one or more funds  that have
 accumulated  for various  proposed  expenditures  (primarily  Capital  Improyement  Projects).

  1  5
 ANALYSIS:  At tonight's  meeting,  which  is the first  of two  scheduled  meetings,  staff  will  provide  a
general  overview  of the Proposed  Budget  for Fiscal  Year  2022-23.  In addition,  several  departments
will  begin  providing  presentations  on their  requested  funding  allocations  for the new fiscal  year.  The
meeting  will  be continued  to August  30,  2022,  where  the Legislative  Bodies  will  hear  from  the
remaining  departments  on their requested  funding  allocations  and will  consider  approving  a Resolution
adopting  the Proposed  Budget  for  Fiscal  Year  2022-23  along  with  any adjustments  discussed  during
these hearings. All these budget meetings  are open to the public  to observe  and participate  through  the
public comment section of the meeting.

The Proposed Budget was placed on the City's webpage for access and review by members of the
public on July 26, 2022. Since then, several adjustments have been identified that need to be made to
the Proposed  Budget  following  reviews  by staff and the City  Council.  These adjustments  to the Budget
are outlined  in Exhibit  A of the attached  resolution.  The General  Fund  proposed  expenditure  budget
increased  by $10,000, wliile  other  special  revenue  and capital  funds  proposed  expenditure  budgets
increased by $2,809,170. The net change to the proposed budget pursuant to these adjustments  total
$2,819,170. The total FY 2022-23 Proposed Budget, to include all funds and entities, with these
adjustments  is $243,580,301. The Proposed  Budget may be further  adjusted with any additions  or
deletions  the Legislative  Bodies  may enact during  the budget  meetings.

It is important  to note that a budget  is a plan that is fluid.  Typically,  reports  on the budget  are made
periodically  during  the fiscal  year.  At  a minimum,  a mid-year  budget  will  be conducted  where  staff
will  report  on the budget  for the current  fiscal  year and request  consideration  of any adjustments  that
may  be needed.  At the same time,  it allows  staff to begin  to solicit  budget  themes  for the upcoming
fiscal year  (FY  2023-24)  that  the City  Council  may  wish  to explore  when  the proposed  budget  is
presented.

BACKGROUND:  A municipal  budget  addresses  city policies,  city operations  and communicates  the
anticipated  financial  activities  to both  the public  and Legislative  Bodies  of the impacted  entities.  This
is the first  of two  scheduled  meetings  to review  the various  proposed  spending  requests.  The second
meeting  will  be on August  30, 2022,  where  the City  Council  will  consider  approving  a Resolution  to
adopt the Proposed  Budget  for Fiscal  Year 2022-23

Government  Code  Section  53901  requires  each local  agency  to file  its budget  with  the county  auditor
within  60 days after the beginning  of its fiscal  year. If an agency  does not have a "formal  budget",  it
must  file  a listing  of its anticipated  revenues  together  with  its expenditures  for  the  fiscal  year  in
progress.

At  the June 28, 2022,  Special  Joint  Meeting  of the City  Council,  Housing  Authority  and Successor
Agency,  the Legislative  Bodies  were  asked to approve  the Continuing  Appropriation  Resolution  until
August  31, 2022,  or the adoption  of the Fiscal  Year  2022-23  Municipal  Budget,  which  ever occurred
first.  Those  resolutions  were unanimously  approved  by each entity.

Additionally,  eacli  year the City  must  adopt  an appropriation  limit  called  the Gann  limit.  The Gann
limit  is designed  to limit  the  amount  of  revenue  that  can  be appropriated  in  a fiscal  year.  The
appropriations  subject  to the limit  are those  that expend  proceeds  of taxes  (e.g.,  Property  Tax,  Sales
Tax,  and Transient  Occupancy  Tax)  less any exclusion  for qualified  capital  outlay,  debt service,  and
federal  mandates.  The finance  staff lias calculated  the Gann Limit  for FY 2022-23  to be $95,725,216,
leaving  the City  with  an appropriations  balance  under  the limit  of $46,606,003.

SECTION  4.  The City  Council  authorizes  the Director  of Administrative  Services  to make  any
budget  appropriations  needed  to carg  out the adopted  labor  agreements  approved  at the regularly
scheduled  City  Council  meeting  conducted  on July 26, 2022.

SUBJECT:  APPROVING  AND  APPROPRIATING  FUNDS  FOR  THE  PURCHASE,
INSTALLATION,  AND  STORAGE  OF CHRISTMAS  DECORATIONS  FOR  A DESIGNATED
AREA  WITHIN  THE  TWEEDY  MILE  BUSINESS  DISTRICT

PURPOSE:  To approve  funding  for the purchase,  installation,  and storage  of Christmas  Decorations
along  a designated  area  on  Tweedy  Boulevard  in  an amount  of  $79,923  and  appropriate  funds
necessary  for the purchase  order.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  the purchase  of Christmas  Decorations  in the amount  of $79,923;  and
  b.  Approving  the appropriation  of $59,923  from  the General  Funds  Reserves  to cover  costs, less
  the $20,000  from  the Tweedy  Mile  Business  Improvement  District  (BID)  Account  #252-120-
  12-6390,  to  complete  the  total  amount  needed  to  purchase  Christmas  decorations  for  a
  designated  area along Tweedy  Boulevard  within  the Tweedy  Mile  Business  District.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The total  needed  to purchase  the holiday  decorations  is $79,923.  Funds  in the
amount  of $20,000  in the Tweedy  Mile  Businesses  Improvement  District  (BID)  budget  will  be used to
pay  for the holiday  decorations.  An  appropriation  of $59,923  from  the General  Fund  is needed  to
cover the difference.

ANALYSIS:  At a previous  Tweedy  Mile  BID  Advisory  Board  meeting,  the board  members  requested
that staff investigate  purchasing  new holiday  decorations  to replace  the ones that are traditionally  hung
along 18 intersections  on Tweedy  Boulevard.  The primary  concern  by the board  members  was that the
existing  decorations  looked  worn  and the lights  had lost  their  luster.  Thus,  the intent  of making  a
special  presentation  during  the holiday  season was being  lost due to the existing  conditions  of those
decorations.

Tlie  existing  garland  strands  strung  across  the Tweedy  Mile  Boulevard  are at least 7 years  old and,
according  to vendors,  liave  exceeded  their  life  expectancy  and should  be replaced.  As  stated,  the
decorations  are strung  across Tweedy  Boulevard  at 18 locations,  all located  within  the boundaries  of
the BID.  Those  boundaries  run  from  Hunt  Ave  and extend  west  to Long  Beach  Boulevard.  The
previous  purchase  of holiday  decorations  was made  using  a portion  of the BID  assessment  fees and
General  Fund dollars.

  17
 The holiday  season  is around  the corner  and due to a supply  shortage,  we have limited  time  to find
Christmas  decorations  for  the  BID.  After  researching  various  options,  staff  is  recommending
purchasing  new  decorations  this  year.  Purchasing  decorations  would  be an investment  because  the
yearly  cost to maintain  them would  be minimal,  costing  just  under  $10,000,  annually,  after the initial
purchase.  The  $10,000  price  includes  storing  the  decorations  throughout  the  year,  installation  in
November,  and removal  in January.  The yearly  contract  would  be paid by BID  funds  in the future.  If
approved,  18  full-lit  green  garlands  with  red  bows  and  wreaths  will  adoin  Tweedy  Boulevard,
beginning  at Hunt  Avenue  and ending  on State Street.

The BID  Advisory  Board  met at a Special  meeting  on August  24, 2022  and recommended  approval
with  a 2-1 vote.

Staff received  pricing  from  the vendor,  Magical  Holiday  Designs.  If 'funding  is approved,  an agreement
will  be presented  to the City  Council  for approval  in a future  meeting.
